faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Clear, honest answers regarding our architectural and civic decisions.
faq.q1: How is ResolveIQ fundamentally different from Zendesk or Freshdesk?
faq.a1: Traditional ticketing systems create individual tickets for every citizen submission. When a water main bursts, 500 citizens create 500 disconnected tickets. ResolveIQ merges them into one Incident with an explainable blast radius, dispatches one municipal crew, and broadcasts updates to all 500 citizens simultaneously.
faq.a2: Over 50 million citizens in Karnataka communicate in Kannada, often mixing Kannada words into Latin characters (Kanglish) on messaging platforms. Western civic tools fail completely on Kanglish. ResolveIQ treats Kannada script and Kanglish as first-class citizens, ensuring democratic access.
faq.q3: Is the SLA risk model trained or rule-based?
faq.a3: By deliberate civic design, the Risk Guard uses a transparent, rule-based formula: risk = 0.4*(elapsed/sla) + 0.3*(load/capacity) + 0.2*(noFirstResponse) + 0.1*(reopens). This ensures explainability in municipal audits without unpredictable black-box drift.
faq.q4: What happens if the AI makes a wrong classification or routing decision?
faq.a4: Every AI decision is accompanied by a confidence score. Any score below 0.60 is automatically routed to the Human Review Queue. Furthermore, all resolution action plans require human supervisor sign-off before dispatch.
faq.q5: Does the system scale to millions of complaints?
faq.a5: Yes. Vector similarity search uses PostgreSQL with pgvector with an ivfflat index, enabling sub-10ms clustering queries across millions of complaints. The FastAPI gateway and asynchronous WebSocket engine support horizontal pod autoscaling.
faq.q6: How is citizen privacy and sensitive data protected?
faq.a6: Citizen phone numbers are strictly masked across all dashboard views except for authorized administrators. File uploads are securely stored in private Cloudflare R2 object storage with time-limited signed URLs that expire after 5 minutes.
